newsitem.title: USA: New York City again to tap Euronote debt market.
newsitem.headline: New York City again to tap Euronote debt market.

text.p: New York City again aims to tap European debt markets, saying Tuesday it planned to sell about $100 million of floating rate Euronotes as part of a bigger refunding set for the week of July 21.

The city, one of the few U.S. localities to sell its taxable debt overseas, also plans to sell $400 million of general obligation, tax-exempt refunding bonds that will have fixed rates, as part of that offering. The sale includes $50 million of taxable, fixed-rate debt.
"So it's all refunding," said a city official, who declined to be named.

The city recently has started selling its taxable debt in Europe, most recently in April, when it placed $50 million bonds there at the same 28-basis point spread over the London Interbank Offered Rate as similar notes it sold in January, even though rates had risen in the interim.
J.P. Morgan & Company will be the bookrunning senior manager for the $400 million bond sale. The syndicate includes Goldman, Sachs & Co and Smith Barney Inc.
Goldman, Sachs will manage the Euronote sale, whose co-manangers include Bear, Stearns, Citibank, J.P. Morgan, Lehman Brothers, Merrill Lynch, Morgan Stanley, and Smith Barney.
How the $50 million sale of fixed-rate, taxable bonds will be handled was not disclosed.
